questions.quote: Average atomic mass of an element is calculated by adding the masses of its isotopes, each multiplied by their natural abundance on the Earth.

en.q: The average atomic mass of an element is calculated by
options: dividing the mass of its heaviest isotope by 12
adding the masses of its isotopes without any weighting
multiplying its atomic number by its mass number
adding the masses of its isotopes each multiplied by its natural abundance
en.explanation: Example: carbon (12.01) from C-12 (98.90 %) and C-13 (1.10 %).

en.q: The number of moles of a substance is equal to
options: mass / molar mass = number of particles / 6.023 × 10²³

questions.quote: Relative atomic mass of an element = mass of one atom of the element / 1/12 of the mass of a C-12 atom. It is denoted as Ar. It is otherwise called 'Standard Atomic Weight'. Relative molecular mass of a molecule is the ratio between the mass of one molecule of the substance to 1/12th of the mass of the atom of carbon-12.

en.q: Which of the following is NOT correct about the relative atomic mass?
options: It is also called the standard atomic weight
It is the ratio of the mass of one atom to 1/12th of a C-12 atom
en.explanation: As a ratio, relative atomic mass has no unit.
